name: Example: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Sine Function
worked_solution:
The period of $y = \sin x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for any integer $n$ we have

$$
\sin{x} = \sin{(x+2n\pi)} .
$$

Substituting $n=3$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+2\cdot 3\cdot \pi ) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+6\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\sin{x} = \dfrac{1}{2},$ then $\sin{(x+6\pi)} = \dfrac{1}{2}.$

Finally, then:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+6\pi )-3 & =-2(\frac{1}{2})-3 \\  & =-1-3 \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$
